_doc: Hand-authored sidecar for UE-side commands routed through HaybaMCPLegacyHandler::Handle (see unreal/HaybaMCPToolkit/Source/HaybaMCPToolkit/Private/handlers/HaybaMCPLegacyHandler.cpp). This file is the single source of truth for: (a) the parameter docs surfaced by get_tool_signature for legacy commands that have no TS Zod registration, and (b) the allowlist that hayba_invoke consults when called with via:'ue_legacy'. INVARIANTS (enforced by scripts/check-legacy-wrappers.ts and CI): every dispatch-table command in the .cpp MUST have an entry here (including aliases); every entry with has_ts_wrapper:true MUST have a corresponding executeCommand('<name>', ...) or dispatch('<name>', ...) call somewhere under src/tools/**; every entry with has_ts_wrapper:false MUST NOT have such a call. To add a new legacy command: register it in the .cpp dispatch table, add an entry here (with aliases array if any), set has_ts_wrapper to whatever's true, run `npm run lint:legacy-wrappers`. Marking agent_callable:false hides it from hayba_invoke via:'ue_legacy' while still letting get_tool_signature document it (e.g. ping, wizard_chat — internal/diagnostic).

Selectors are case-insensitive and cannot be combined with explicit names; an empty or zero-match selection is an error rather than a false green run. Poll build_status for { passed, failed, skipped, elapsed_seconds, total }, or test_get_log for detailed entries. data_create.notes: Create and persist a concrete, current UDataAsset subclass after bounded path/name/class preflight. MarkPackageDirty and SaveLoadedAsset are callback boundaries: no raw creation pointer crosses either one, and the target path/class is freshly re-resolved before save and again afterward. Inspect ok, dirty_marked, pre_save_re_resolved, save_attempted, saved (present only when attempted), target_re_resolved, and dirty_known. If any identity, dirty-mark, save, or final readback fact is not trustworthy, nested ok:false plus data_create_unknown_outcome makes the top-level response unknown_outcome; query the exact path before retrying.

data_get.notes: Read a bounded property snapshot from a DataAsset. Always inspect reflection_complete, reflection_truncated, properties_omitted_at_least, unsupported_values, and large_integers_as_strings before treating it as complete. Set/map item counts and physical sparse-slot ranges are both capped before iteration, so a small live count cannot hide an unbounded hole scan. Integers outside the exact JSON-number range are decimal strings, never rounded. Soft, weak, lazy, and soft-class wrapper references are reported unsupported/partial instead of falsely serializing an unloaded non-null path as null. Properties with native getters or setters are also unsupported/partial: raw bytes may not be their logical value, and invoking an accessor would execute unaudited code.

data_set.notes: Write one bounded scalar property on a DataAsset by name, then inspect copy_completed, ok, verified, target_re_resolved, dirty_marked, dirty_known, dirty (when known), and observed_value or observed_value_omitted. Only exact built-in numeric, enum, bool, string, and name property classes without native getters/setters are accepted and assigned through direct typed setters; JsonValueToUProperty and ImportText are never entered. Fixed arrays, dynamic containers, structs (including user-defined structs), wrapper/object references, interfaces, delegates, optionals, text, field paths, SkipSerialization fields, accessor-backed fields, custom property subclasses, and every other extensible type are refused before staging. Staging and all property pointers end before dirty notification; the command then re-resolves the target/class/property and repeats the accessor/schema gate before fresh bounded readback. It deliberately skips transactions, UObject editor hooks, and persistence. save_requested is always false. If any final identity/verification/dirty fact is untrustworthy, nested ok:false plus stable error makes the top-level response unknown_outcome with mandatory readback; ErrorsOnly cannot hide it.

level_create.notes: Create a new empty level asset. Does not open it — follow with level_load to switch the editor to it.

level_save.notes: Save the current level, or the one at `path`. Editor edits live in memory until this runs, so an unsaved level loses everything on restart or a rebuild.

level_load.notes: Open a level in the editor, replacing the current one. UNSAVED CHANGES IN THE CURRENT LEVEL ARE AT RISK — call level_save first.

level_list.notes: List every level asset in the project. Use it to find the exact path level_load wants.

level_get_info.notes: Name and actor count of the level currently open. The cheapest way to confirm which level you are actually editing before making changes.

asset_registry_query.notes: Native, read-only AssetRegistry discovery with class/name/path filters and deterministic bounded pagination. Returns package paths, not object paths.

asset_search.notes: Find assets by path, name substring or class, optionally with thumbnails. The general 'what exists in this project' query — start here when you need an asset path and only know roughly what it is.

asset_get_info.notes: Read one asset's metadata (class, path, size, optional thumbnail) by exact path. Use asset_search when you do not yet know the path.

params.name: source_file
params.description: One absolute regular file below the fixed OS-temp/hayba-asset-connectors source/request cache. Links, reparse points, hardlinks, device/UNC paths, traversal, and files outside that authority are rejected.

params.name: destination_path
params.description: Canonical /Game folder. The exact asset name is the strict ASCII source basename; an existing registry/live/disk package is refused, never overwritten.

params.name: asset_type
params.description: Exact type intent: texture for PNG/JPEG, sound_wave for WAV, or static_mesh for binary FBX. glTF/GLB/OBJ/USD and dependency-reading formats are rejected.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable HAI_* result/refusal code.

fields.name: mutation_status
fields.description: not_started, applied_unsaved/applied, partially_applied, or unknown.

fields.name: failure_kind
fields.description: Machine-actionable refusal/retry/unknown/session classification on failure.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Exact freshly AssetRegistry-read object path; present only on verified success.

fields.name: class
fields.description: Exact freshly AssetRegistry-read class.

fields.name: verified
fields.description: True only after exact object path, package, asset name, class, and live package re-resolution.

fields.name: saved
fields.description: Whether the exact package is present on disk after import; asset_import itself does not request a save.

fields.name: save_attempted
fields.description: Always false: asset_import deliberately leaves persistence to an explicit asset_save call.

fields.name: dirty_known
fields.description: Whether dirty is backed by a freshly re-resolved live package.

fields.name: dirty
fields.description: Fresh live-package dirty state; interpret only with dirty_known.

fields.name: partial
fields.description: Failure fact: some mutation evidence exists despite failed exact readback.

fields.name: unknown_outcome
fields.description: Failure fact: callbacks returned without proof of one exact result; do not retry unchanged.

fields.name: session_suspect
fields.description: True for impossible return/readback invariants or unexpected returned outputs; stop further mutations and restart/inspect.

fields.name: crafted_format_safety
fields.description: Always not_proven: bounded header checks cannot contain an in-process engine parser.

asset_import.notes: Fail-closed, single-file native import. It pins the fixed connector-cache ancestor/file handles, enforces kind-specific size+magic policy and an exact factory, refuses collisions/overwrite, then discards callback-returned UObject pointers and re-resolves the exact registry path/class/package. Successful imports are normally dirty_in_memory: follow with asset_save on the returned exact path. These checks reduce exposure but do NOT prove crafted files safe for an in-process UE parser; untrusted remote files still require an isolated sanitizer. Future connector continuation additionally requires an opaque single-use grant bound to one enumerated file; directory assertions are not authority.

asset_duplicate.notes: Copy an asset to a new path. Use this to derive a variant rather than editing the original in place.

params.name: location
params.description: World-space camera position [x, y, z] in cm.

params.name: look_at
params.description: BEST way to aim the camera: a world point [x,y,z] to face. The orientation is computed in C++ (correct pitch+yaw, roll always 0 — the horizon never tilts). Use this instead of rotation whenever you know what you want the camera pointed at; you do NOT compute any angles yourself. Takes precedence over rotation.

params.name: rotation
params.description: Manual orientation (only if you are not using look_at). PREFERRED form: object {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees — unambiguous. yaw = heading (about the vertical/Z axis, the value you usually want); pitch = look up(+)/down(-); roll = horizon tilt and defaults to 0 (omit it — a non-zero roll is what makes the viewport 'look angled'). Array form is accepted as [pitch, yaw, roll] but its 3rd element (roll) is IGNORED so the camera never tilts by accident — do NOT pass [x,y,z] euler here, index 2 is roll, not yaw.

fields.name: location
fields.description: Applied [x,y,z]

fields.name: rotation
fields.description: Applied [pitch, yaw, roll]

editor_set_camera.notes: Position the editor viewport camera for deterministic captures. To AIM it, prefer look_at:[x,y,z] (orientation computed for you, never tilts). Manual rotation is UE FRotator (pitch/yaw/roll), NOT xyz-euler. To simply frame an actor, use editor_focus_actor instead.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Label of the actor to frame in the viewport.

params.name: distance_scale
params.description: How far back to sit, as a multiple of the actor's bounds radius (default 2.5; larger = further/more padding).

params.name: direction
params.description: Optional [x,y,z] view direction (camera→actor). Default is a 3/4 front-right-above view. Need not be normalized.

fields.name: location
fields.description: Resulting camera [x,y,z]

fields.name: rotation
fields.description: Resulting [pitch, yaw, roll] (roll always 0)

editor_focus_actor.notes: Frame an actor in the editor viewport by label — computes camera position from the actor's bounds and aims at its centre, entirely in C++. Roll is always 0 so the view never tilts. This is the correct 'framing tool'; do NOT hand-compute camera angles in python_run.

params.name: quit
params.description: Set false to save and verify without scheduling editor exit

fields.name: dirty_package_count_after
fields.description: Always zero on success

editor_save_all_and_quit.notes: Single native persistence boundary used by the first-class TS tool: persist every loaded dirty map/content package, verify none remain, then optionally schedule editor exit after the response flushes. Exit revalidates dirtiness and cancels if queued/background work changed state. Refuses queued or active PIE and any save failure. Plan-Mode gated and non-idempotent when quit is true.

editor_run_console_command.notes: Run an editor console command (stat unit, r.* toggles, LiveCoding.Compile, etc). Arbitrary console access, so it is gated by Plan Mode. Effects are reported by the console, not returned — check editor_get_output_log.

editor_get_output_log.notes: Read the editor's output log, filtered by severity or regex and paged with since_line. The first thing to check when a command reported success but nothing happened — UE logs the real reason here.

editor_stop_pie.notes: Stop the running Play-In-Editor session and return whether one was running. Call it before editor-only operations: many asset and level edits are unsafe or refused while PIE is live.

params.name: widget_blueprint_path
params.description: Widget Blueprint asset path, for example /Game/UI/WBP_HUD

params.name: widget_name
params.description: Exact widget name in the authoritative designer WidgetTree

params.name: properties
params.description: Widget UPROPERTY names mapped to reflection-compatible values

params.name: slot_props
params.description: Optional typed slot values such as x, y, w, h, padding, and fill

ui_set_widget_properties.notes: Edits the authoritative UWidgetBlueprint designer tree and survives compilation when followed by ui_compile_widget and ui_save_widget. Reached through the ui_set_widget_properties TS wrapper and the typed tools (ui_set_property, ui_set_text_style, ui_set_brush, ui_set_visibility, ui_set_slot_layout) that compose onto it.

scene_get_actor_relations.notes: Report one actor's attachment parent, its attached children and its asset references. Answers 'what would move or break if I reparent or delete this' — it is not an inventory, use actor_list for that.

params.name: filename
params.description: Absolute PNG output path; defaults to Saved/Screenshots/HaybaPIE_<timestamp>.png. Captures the composited PIE viewport INCLUDING UMG (unlike HighResShot).

fields.name: filename
fields.description: path written

fields.name: captured
fields.description: true if the file exists after capture

editor_pie_screenshot.notes: Requests a capture and returns immediately; the engine writes the file a frame or two later. Poll with check_only:true. Previously pumped the core ticker for up to 3s from the game thread, which crashed the editor.

params.name: key
params.description: FKey name, e.g. 'A','Enter','Tab','SpaceBar','LeftMouseButton'

params.name: event
params.description: 'Pressed' (default), 'Released', or a down+up click depending on handler

params.name: held_ms
params.description: Hold duration in ms before release

editor_pie_press_key.notes: Dispatches the press and schedules the release on a later tick, returning immediately. Previously spun the core ticker while holding raw viewport pointers, which tore down PIE underneath itself and crashed.

params.name: action
params.description: move|click|double|press|release|drag|scroll

params.name: x
params.description: target x, ABSOLUTE desktop px by default (what editor_pie_widget_tree reports) — see coordinate_space. Optional for scroll: positions the cursor before the wheel.

params.name: y
params.description: target y, ABSOLUTE desktop px by default (what editor_pie_widget_tree reports) — see coordinate_space. Optional for scroll: positions the cursor before the wheel.

params.name: coordinate_space
params.description: absolute (default, desktop px) | viewport (relative to the game window's top-left)

params.name: button
params.description: Left|Right|Middle (default Left)

params.name: to_x
params.description: drag end x

params.name: to_y
params.description: drag end y

params.name: steps
params.description: intermediate drag positions (default 8, clamped 1..256)

params.name: delta
params.description: wheel notches for scroll (default 1, positive scrolls up)

fields.name: cursor_delta_x
fields.description: FPointerEvent::GetCursorDelta of the last move dispatched. ZERO means no widget that tracks movement can have responded — that is a harness result, not a widget result.

fields.name: cursor_delta_y
fields.description: As cursor_delta_x.

fields.name: moves_delivered
fields.description: How many moves carried a non-zero delta. 0 on a drag means no gesture was performed.

fields.name: mouse_captor
fields.description: Type name of the widget holding Slate pointer capture after the action, or null. A drag against a null captor cannot work: SScrollBar::OnMouseMove and friends gate on HasMouseCapture().

fields.name: captor_after_press
fields.description: drag only — who took capture in answer to the press.

fields.name: pressed_buttons
fields.description: Slate's held mouse buttons after the action. Moves between a press and a release carry this set, which is what SScrollBox's right-click drag scrolling reads.

fields.name: handled_by
fields.description: scroll only — slate | game_viewport | nothing.

editor_pie_mouse.notes: Move, click, double_click, press, release, drag or scroll in the running game. All of it is synthesised as real Slate FPointerEvents, so UI widgets see it: the wheel goes through ProcessMouseWheelOrGestureEvent (it used to go to game input only and reached no widget at all), and drag moves carry the held button plus a genuine non-zero cursor delta (they used to carry neither, because SetCursorPos writes the destination to Slate's previous-position slot too, so every synthetic move had a zero delta). Judge a gesture by cursor_delta/moves_delivered/mouse_captor in the response, not by assuming it landed.

params.name: text
params.description: text to type as character events (what text fields consume)

editor_pie_type_text.notes: Sends character events, which is what text fields consume. Goes to whatever holds keyboard focus.

params.name: match
params.description: visible text/label of the widget to click; prefers the interactive widget

editor_pie_click_widget.notes: Clicks a control by its visible text, tag or type, preferring the interactive widget. Reports candidate count so an ambiguous pick is visible.

params.name: max_depth
params.description: limit tree depth

params.name: filter
params.description: substring filter on text/type/tag

editor_pie_widget_tree.notes: Every visible Slate/UMG widget in the running game with its on-screen rectangle. The input to click-by-name.

params.name: key
params.description: axis FKey, e.g. Gamepad_LeftX

params.name: value
params.description: axis value -1..1

editor_pie_axis.notes: Analog input for sticks, triggers and mouse axes. Applies for one frame; resend per step for sustained movement.

fields.name: project_dir
fields.description: Absolute path, forward slashes

fields.name: saved_dir
fields.description: Where the editor log lives — the first place to look when a command claims success

project_get_info.notes: Where this project is on disk and which engine built it. Call it before any path-building work rather than guessing a content root, and to resolve the Saved/ directory the editor log lives in. Takes no parameters.

fields.name: editor_startup_map
fields.description: Read from GEngineIni, not from GeneralProjectSettings

project_get_settings.notes: Reads UGeneralProjectSettings — the identity fields shown on the Project Settings > Description page — plus the editor startup map. Read-only; use project_set_settings to change any of them. Fields that were never filled in come back as empty strings, not as missing keys.

params.name: section
params.description: Raw-ini mode: the ini section, e.g. /Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings. Requires key and value; writes GEngineIni and takes precedence over the named fields below.

params.name: key
params.description: Raw-ini mode: the ini key. Only with section + value.

params.name: value
params.description: Raw-ini mode: the value to write. Only with section + key.

params.name: project_name
params.description: Named mode: written to DefaultGame.ini

fields.name: updated
fields.description: Named mode: exactly which fields were written. Check it — a field this command does not recognise is not reported per-key.

fields.name: section
fields.description: Raw-ini mode only

fields.name: key
fields.description: Raw-ini mode only

project_set_settings.notes: Writes project identity settings to the ini files, in two modes: pass section+key+value to write any ini key directly, or pass any of the named fields to write DefaultGame.ini. It flushes to disk immediately — this edits config the whole team shares, so prefer project_get_settings first. Values are strings in both modes.

fields.name: plugins
fields.description: name, friendly_name, version, version_name, enabled, category, description, is_engine

project_list_plugins.notes: Every ENABLED plugin, engine and project alike, with its version and category. This is the reliable way to answer 'is Water/PCG/Niagara available here' before calling a domain that needs one — a capability probe against reality rather than an assumption. Disabled plugins are not listed at all.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of a UStaticMesh, e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube.Cube

fields.name: lod_screen_sizes
fields.description: One entry per source model, in LOD order

fields.name: material_slots
fields.description: name + material_path per slot; material_path is empty when the slot has no material

fields.name: bounds
fields.description: min / max / extents, each {x,y,z}

mesh_get_info.notes: Triangle and vertex counts, the LOD chain with its screen sizes, material slots and local bounds for one static mesh. Called from TS by the physical-asset baker and world_generate for bounds, so it is documented here rather than surfaced as its own agent tool: agents should reach for mesh_get_bounds / mesh_get_lods / mesh_get_materials, which split the same information and do not load the asset whole.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of the UStaticMesh

params.name: lod_index
params.description: Which source model; must be within lod_count from mesh_get_info

params.name: screen_size
params.description: Screen size at which this LOD takes over

params.name: reduction_percent_triangles
params.description: Optional triangle-reduction target for this LOD

mesh_set_lod.notes: Sets a LOD's screen size (and optionally its reduction target) on a static mesh, then rebuilds it. Editor-only, and it modifies the asset — save it afterwards. It REFUSES a mesh with any zero-UV LOD, because the rebuild would hit an engine assert and take the editor down with it; that refusal is a real limit of the asset, not a bug in this command.

params.name: path_prefix
params.description: Keep only assets whose object path starts with this, e.g. /Game/Aphrosia. Omitted means every static mesh the registry knows, engine content included.

fields.name: meshes
fields.description: path, name, package_path

mesh_list.notes: Enumerate static meshes from the asset registry without loading any of them — the cheap way to find something to place or inspect. Always pass path_prefix on a real project unless you actually want engine content in the results. Exact subclasses only, so a mesh subclass is not listed.

params.name: path_prefix
params.description: Keep only sounds whose object path starts with this. Omitted means everything, including the large engine sound set.

fields.name: sounds
fields.description: path, name, class, and duration_seconds / sample_rate when the registry has them cached

audio_list.notes: Enumerate USoundBase assets (waves, cues, MetaSound sources) from the asset registry, including subclasses, without loading them. Duration and sample rate come from registry tags, so they are present for most assets but not guaranteed — a missing key means untagged, not zero.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of a USoundBase

params.name: start_time
params.description: Playback seek offset in seconds

params.name: concurrency_path
params.description: Optional SoundConcurrency override

fields.name: component_id
fields.description: Stable retained AudioComponent id, controllable with audio_component_control

audio_play.notes: Play a sound 2D through a retained AudioComponent. Fails unless the component becomes active and returns component_id plus live play-state/volume/pitch readback. Prefer audio_component_play for the fully typed first-class schema.

params.name: category
params.description: Only 'master' is implemented; any other category is an explicit error rather than a silent no-op

params.name: volume
params.description: Multiplier, 1.0 being unchanged

audio_set_volume.notes: Sets the transient primary volume on the main audio device — the master bus, and only that. Use audio_asset_create/set/save with SoundClass and SoundMix assets for category routing. The change is transient and does not persist.

params.name: path
params.description: Full /Game target asset path; package-only/object/export-text forms normalize identically

params.name: asset_type
params.description: SoundClass|SoundMix|SoundConcurrency|SoundAttenuation|SoundSubmix

audio_asset_create.notes: Creates an unsaved audio settings asset with a typed default readback. SoundWave is engine-limited here because it needs imported PCM data: use asset_import then audio_asset_set. Explicitly call audio_asset_save after authoring.

params.name: path
params.description: Supported audio asset path

audio_asset_inspect.notes: Typed inspection for SoundClass, SoundMix/class overrides, SoundConcurrency, SoundAttenuation, SoundSubmix, and SoundWave import/playback policy.

params.name: settings
params.description: Typed snake_case settings documented by the first-class Zod schema; incompatible keys fail before mutation

audio_asset_set.notes: Set-to-value audio authoring with changed/unchanged diagnostics and full readback. Mutates memory only; audio_asset_save is the explicit persistence boundary.

audio_asset_save.notes: Single-target explicit save. It verifies the .uasset exists on disk and fails rather than reporting nested saved:false.

audio_component_play.notes: Starts retained, controllable 2D playback and fails unless playback becomes active.

params.name: action
params.description: play|stop|pause|resume|fade_in|fade_out|set_volume|set_pitch|set_parameter|reset_parameters

audio_component_control.notes: Controls retained AudioComponents and typed SoundCue/MetaSound parameters. Expired ids and failed replays are errors.

audio_active_sounds.notes: Reads active sounds and physical voice count from the main audio device for concurrency, virtualization, and leak diagnosis.

params.name: submix_path
params.description: Omit for master output

audio_meter_start.notes: Starts tracked Audio Mixer spectral analysis; fails cleanly on a non-mixer device or duplicate target.

params.name: frequencies_hz
params.description: 1..256 frequencies in (0,24000]

audio_meter_read.notes: Reads linear magnitude, dB magnitude, and phase. No analyzer or no spectral data is an error, not zero-filled success.

audio_meter_stop.notes: Stops a tracked master/submix analyzer; no active analyzer is an error.

audio_recording_start.notes: Starts tracked Audio Mixer capture of master or one submix; fails cleanly when Audio Mixer is unavailable.

params.name: relative_path
params.description: Subfolder under Saved/BouncedWavFiles; absolute/.. rejected

audio_recording_stop.notes: Stops capture and uses UE's synchronous PCM writer. Zero samples, writer failure, or absent WAV is an outer command error.

params.name: enabled
params.description: true turns the net stat overlay and packet-handler logging on, false turns both off

params.name: channels
params.description: Reported back as channels_applied. Defaults to ["all"]. Currently descriptive only — the same overlay is enabled whatever you pass.

net_debug.notes: Toggles the networking stat overlay (stat net) and packet-handler log stats in the editor viewport. Reach for it when diagnosing replication during PIE. It is a viewport overlay, so the effect is visible in a screenshot rather than in this reply; the reply only tells you the console commands were issued.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Actor name, label, or full object path in the current editor world

params.name: replicate
params.description: Whether the actor replicates at all

params.name: always_relevant
params.description: Left alone when omitted, rather than reset to false

params.name: net_dormancy
params.description: Awake | Initial | DormantAll. DORM_Never and DORM_DormantPartial cannot be expressed — an unrecognised value is rejected and nothing is written.

params.name: replicated_components
params.description: Component names to mark replicated. Ones that do not resolve come back under missing_components rather than being dropped.

fields.name: actor
fields.description: Full object path of the actor that was actually matched

fields.name: replicates
fields.description: Read back off the actor, not echoed from the request

fields.name: always_relevant
fields.description: Present only when you passed it

fields.name: net_dormancy
fields.description: Present only when you passed it

fields.name: missing_components
fields.description: Names that matched no component on the actor

net_set_replication.notes: Sets replication flags on one actor in the editor world and marks its level dirty — this edits the LEVEL, so the change persists only if the level is saved, and it is not something to try on a map someone is working in. Every parameter is validated before anything is written, so a rejected request leaves the actor untouched.

params.name: path
params.description: Package folder, e.g. /Game/Input

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name. A name already in use is refused rather than overwritten.

params.name: value_type
params.description: Boolean | Axis1D | Axis2D | Axis3D

fields.name: path
fields.description: Full object path of the created UInputAction

input_create_action.notes: Creates an Enhanced Input UInputAction — the 'what the player did' half of the system, independent of which key does it. Pick value_type by the shape of the input: Boolean for a press, Axis1D for a trigger, Axis2D for a stick. The asset is created dirty and unsaved; call asset_save to keep it. An existing name is an explicit error, because letting the engine ask would raise a modal dialog and hang every queued command.

params.name: path
params.description: Package folder, e.g. /Game/Input

params.name: name
params.description: Asset name; an existing one is refused, not overwritten

fields.name: path
fields.description: Full object path of the created UInputMappingContext

input_create_mapping.notes: Creates an empty UInputMappingContext — the 'which keys, in this situation' half of Enhanced Input. A context is what gets pushed and popped as the player moves between menus, driving and walking. Fill it with input_add_mapping. Created dirty and unsaved; asset_save to keep it.

params.name: mapping_path
params.description: Object path of an existing UInputMappingContext

params.name: action_path
params.description: Object path of an existing UInputAction

params.name: key_name
params.description: Engine key name, e.g. W, SpaceBar, Gamepad_LeftX. An unknown key is rejected.

params.name: modifiers
params.description: UInputModifier class names, e.g. InputModifierNegate, InputModifierSwizzleAxis

params.name: triggers
params.description: UInputTrigger class names, e.g. InputTriggerPressed, InputTriggerHold

fields.name: modifiers
fields.description: The ones actually constructed and attached

fields.name: unresolved_classes
fields.description: Names that matched no modifier/trigger class. The binding is still made — check this before believing a modifier applied.

input_add_mapping.notes: Binds a key to an action inside a mapping context, optionally with modifiers and triggers. A modifier or trigger class name it cannot resolve is reported under unresolved_classes rather than silently skipped — so a reply listing fewer modifiers than you asked for is telling you something. Marks the context dirty; asset_save to keep it.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of a UBehaviorTree

fields.name: root_class
fields.description: Empty on a tree that has no root node yet

fields.name: nodes
fields.description: guid, name, class, parent_guid, children — the guid is derived from the node's object path, so it is stable across calls

bt_get_info.notes: Reads a behavior tree's whole node graph plus its blackboard keys. Call it first: bt_add_node and bt_connect address nodes by the guids this returns, and those guids come from node object paths rather than being stored, so they stay valid between calls without any bookkeeping on your side.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of the UBehaviorTree

params.name: node_kind
params.description: composite | task | decorator | service. Checked against the class — asking for a composite and naming a task class is an error, not a guess.

params.name: node_class_name
params.description: UBTNode subclass, e.g. BTComposite_Selector, BTTask_Wait, BTDecorator_Blackboard

params.name: parent_guid
params.description: From bt_get_info. Omitted on a composite means it becomes the root; decorators and services always need a composite parent.

fields.name: guid
fields.description: Address the new node by this in bt_connect

bt_add_node.notes: Adds one node to a behavior tree. Build a tree root-first: a composite with no parent_guid becomes the root, then tasks and further composites hang off it by guid. The kind/class mismatch checks are strict on purpose, since a decorator quietly added as a task is the kind of thing you only notice when the AI misbehaves. Marks the asset dirty; asset_save to keep it.

params.name: parent_guid
params.description: Must be a composite — only composites take children

params.name: child_guid
params.description: A composite or a task

bt_connect.notes: Re-parents an existing node under a composite. It refuses to connect a node to itself and refuses an edge that would make a cycle, so a tree cannot be wired into one that never terminates. Ordering among siblings is the order children were added, and that order is execution order for a Selector or Sequence.

fields.name: warnings
fields.description: e.g. "Behavior tree has no blackboard asset" — a tree that compiles clean can still be one that cannot run

bt_compile.notes: Compiles the tree and reports what the compiler said. Read the warnings, not just ok: a tree with no blackboard asset compiles successfully and then does nothing useful at runtime, and that case is reported as a warning rather than an error.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of a UAnimBlueprint

fields.name: target_skeleton
fields.description: Empty string when the asset genuinely has no skeleton bound

fields.name: state_machines
fields.description: Each with its name, states and transitions

anim_blueprint_get_info.notes: Reads an animation blueprint's state machines, their states and transitions, and its variables. Call it before any of the anim_blueprint_* writers: they address a state machine BY NAME, and this is the only way to learn the names — a freshly created anim blueprint has none at all.

params.name: state_machine_name
params.description: From anim_blueprint_get_info. This command does not create state machines — only states inside one that exists.

params.name: new_state_name
params.description: A name already used in that state machine is refused rather than duplicated

anim_blueprint_add_state.notes: Adds a state to an existing state machine in an animation blueprint. It cannot create the state machine itself — that still needs the AnimGraph editor — so on a blueprint with none it answers 'state machine not found', which is a missing prerequisite rather than a bad request. Compile with anim_blueprint_compile afterwards.

params.name: state_machine_name
params.description: Optional — without it the states are searched for across every state machine, which is ambiguous if two share a state name

fields.name: transition_id
fields.description: Pass to anim_blueprint_set_condition

anim_blueprint_add_transition.notes: Wires one state to another. The transition is created with no rule, which means it is always taken — pair it with anim_blueprint_set_condition unless you actually want an unconditional transition. Pass state_machine_name when two state machines might share a state name.

params.name: condition_expression
params.description: The rule to drive the transition

params.name: transition_id
params.description: From anim_blueprint_add_transition. Use this, or from_state + to_state.

anim_blueprint_set_condition.notes: Sets the rule on an existing transition, identified either by its id or by the pair of states it joins. A transition with no rule fires immediately, so this is what turns a wired-up state machine into one that behaves. Compile afterwards to find out whether the expression resolved.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Raw EBlueprintStatus; 3 is up-to-date

anim_blueprint_compile.notes: Compiles an ANIMATION blueprint (ABP) — the animation state-machine asset, not an ordinary class. Reports the compiler errors and warnings. Every anim_blueprint_* write leaves the asset needing this, and an uncompiled ABP keeps running its previously generated class, so state-machine edits look like they did nothing.

params.name: actor_id
params.description: Actor name or editor label in the current editor world

params.name: component_name
params.description: Which primitive component. Omitted means the root component, falling back to the first primitive component found.

fields.name: simulating
fields.description: Read back off the component after the write, not echoed — a component that refused to simulate reports false here

physics_set_simulate.notes: Turns rigid-body simulation on or off for one primitive component in the EDITOR world. The reply reads the flag back off the component rather than repeating the request, so a component that cannot simulate (no collision, no body instance) is visible as simulating:false with ok:true. Editor-world only: this is not how you drive physics during PIE.

params.name: profile_name
params.description: A profile from Project Settings > Collision, e.g. BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision

params.name: component_name
params.description: Defaults to the root primitive component

fields.name: requested_profile
fields.description: What you asked for

fields.name: profile
fields.description: What the component is actually on, read back after the write

physics_set_collision_profile.notes: Assigns a named collision profile to one primitive component and READS IT BACK. An unrecognised name leaves the component on whatever it had, so a mismatch between requested_profile and profile is returned as an error naming the current setting rather than as a success. Names come from the project Collision settings, e.g. BlockAll, NoCollision, Pawn. This SETS a profile; to find out what is currently intersecting what, use scene_validate_physics.

params.name: impulse
params.description: [x,y,z]. Fewer than three numbers is rejected rather than zero-filled.

params.name: velocity_change
params.description: true applies the vector as a velocity change, ignoring mass

fields.name: linear_velocity
fields.description: {x,y,z} read off the body after the impulse — an observable to compare against what you asked for

physics_add_impulse.notes: Applies an impulse to a primitive component in the editor world and reports the resulting linear velocity. A component that is not simulating physics discards an impulse silently, so that case is REFUSED with a message naming the fix rather than answering applied:true — the old reply was true of the call and false of the world. Turn simulation on with physics_set_simulate first.

fields.name: cells
fields.description: cell_id, bounds{min,max}, actor_count, top_classes (top 5 by count)

fields.name: total
fields.description: How many cells exist

fields.name: returned
fields.description: Present only when the list was cut short at 100

fields.name: truncated
fields.description: Present only when total exceeds what was returned

fields.name: cell_source
fields.description: Always "computed_grid" — see the note

fields.name: grid_size_cm
fields.description: The fixed bin size used, 51200

wp_get_cells.notes: A spatial summary of where actors are: it bins every actor in the editor world onto a fixed 512m grid and reports per-bin counts and the classes that dominate each. These are NOT the World Partition runtime cells — cell ids and bounds will not match the partition's own, which is why the reply says cell_source. Requires World Partition to be enabled on the map; use it to find the busy regions before deciding where to look.

params.name: cell_id
params.description: Accepted and ignored — the command cannot load anything

wp_load_cell.notes: NOT IMPLEMENTED, and it says so rather than pretending: World Partition cell loading is interactive-only in the editor, so every call returns an error naming that limit. It previously returned ok with loaded:false, which let a caller loop over cells and conclude the world was loaded. agent_callable:false — an honest error is still a command that can never succeed, and the catalogue should not offer it.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Whether the current editor world has a World Partition at all

fields.name: streaming_sources
fields.description: Always "not_enumerated" — sources are not counted here, and the field says so rather than reporting a zero that would read as measured

wp_get_streaming_state.notes: Answers one question honestly: does the current editor world use World Partition. It previously also reported a hard-coded source_count of 0 — a field named for a measurement that always answers zero reads as "measured, none found", so it now names itself not_enumerated instead of inventing a number.

fields.name: fps
fields.description: Engine rolling average

fields.name: render_thread_ms
fields.description: Converted from engine cycles

fields.name: game_thread_ms
fields.description: Converted from engine cycles

editor_get_performance_stats.notes: Editor frame timing: average fps, frame time, and the two thread times. These are whole-editor averages, not a profile of one operation — an idle editor with a compile running reads badly and that is not a scene problem. The thread times are cycle counters converted through FPlatformTime::ToMilliseconds; they were previously emitted RAW under _ms names, so every reading of those two fields used to be wrong by the platform cycle factor.

fields.name: compile_requested
fields.description: The trigger was issued. NOT that the compile succeeded — the outcome never comes back through this call.

fields.name: result_source
fields.description: Where to read the actual outcome

fields.name: log_dir
fields.description: Absolute project log directory

editor_live_compile.notes: Triggers a Live Coding compile of the running editor. It is asynchronous: poll the editor log for 'Live coding succeeded' or 'LogLiveCoding: Error', matching on a COUNT of terminal lines rather than presence, because earlier runs are still in the file. Compile ERRORS are not in the editor log at all — they are in UnrealBuildTool\Log.txt. A brand-new handler CLASS still needs a full editor restart; Live Coding cannot register one.

params.name: mode
params.description: lit | unlit | wireframe | detail_lighting | lighting_only | shader_complexity

editor_set_viewport_mode.notes: Switches the active editor viewport's view mode — wireframe to read geometry density, shader_complexity to find expensive materials, unlit to judge albedo without lighting. This changes what a HUMAN is looking at and does not change back on its own, so put it back to lit when you are done rather than leaving someone else's viewport in wireframe.

params.name: class_path
params.description: Class you intend to spawn, e.g. /Script/Engine.StaticMeshActor

params.name: location
params.description: [x,y,z] of the intended placement. A short array is an error, not a silent zero — a 2-element location once made this report a clean spot at the origin.

params.name: rotation
params.description: [pitch,yaw,roll]

params.name: scale
params.description: [x,y,z]

fields.name: valid
fields.description: True when nothing overlaps the intended placement

fields.name: overlaps
fields.description: id + class of each actor already occupying the space

placement_validate.notes: Asks whether an actor of this class would collide with anything if spawned at this transform, WITHOUT spawning it. Use it before actor_spawn when placing into a populated scene — cheaper than spawning, checking, and deleting. It answers about overlap only: it does not tell you whether the spot makes sense, is on navmesh, or is inside geometry.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of the UBlueprint

params.name: function_name
params.description: A name already used by this blueprint is NOT rejected — see the note

fields.name: compiled_clean
fields.description: READ THIS. False means the function was added and the blueprint no longer compiles.

fields.name: compile_errors
fields.description: Present when the compile failed

blueprint_add_function.notes: Adds an empty function graph to a blueprint and recompiles. Check compiled_clean, not just ok: adding a function whose name is already taken SUCCEEDS and leaves the blueprint broken with 'Found more than one function with the same name' — verified live. The reply reports the compiler's verdict, but the operation is not rolled back, so a duplicate name costs you a manual repair.

params.name: path
params.description: Object path of the UBlueprint

fields.name: documentation
fields.description: One WHEN ... THEN ... line per event, e.g. "WHEN Event BeginPlay THEN END"

blueprint_document.notes: Renders a blueprint's EVENT GRAPH as pseudo-English — a fast way to see what a blueprint reacts to without opening it. It covers events only: user-defined function graphs do not appear, so a blueprint documented as three bare events may still have functions. Use blueprint_get_info for structure.

blueprint_inspect_graph.notes: Read-only exact graph export. Returns stable node GUIDs, pin names/directions/types, every edge, counts, and dirty state. Use this before adding or wiring nodes.

params.name: node_type
params.description: call_function, branch, select, timer_by_function, variable_get, variable_set, or cast

blueprint_add_node.notes: Stages a standard event-graph node and returns its GUID plus exact pins. timer_by_function creates K2_SetTimer; set its Object, FunctionName, Time and Looping pins before compile.

blueprint_connect_nodes.notes: Wires exec or data pins using GUIDs and exact pin names from blueprint_inspect_graph/add_node. The K2 schema rejects invalid type or direction connections.

blueprint_set_pin_default.notes: Sets a literal or object/class reference on an unconnected input pin. Refuses connected pins so values are never silently ignored.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Always "deferred"

fields.name: see
fields.description: Always "scene_export"

level_get_spatial_index.notes: NOT IMPLEMENTED — returns status:"deferred" pointing at scene_export, for every call. Documented here so get_tool_signature can explain it, but agent_callable:false so it does not appear as capability an agent can spend a turn discovering is empty. Use scene_export, or wp_get_cells for a spatial summary.

params.name: name
params.description: Bookmark identifier

params.name: location
params.description: [x,y,z]; defaults to the current viewport camera position when omitted

params.name: rotation
params.description: [pitch,yaw,roll]

level_set_bookmark.notes: Stores a named camera position in the current level so it can be returned to later. Bookmarks live in the LEVEL, so this dirties the map and persists only if the level is saved — do not use it as scratch state on a map someone else is working in. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: described from the handler source, because verifying it means dirtying a real level.

params.name: name
params.description: A bookmark previously stored by level_set_bookmark

level_goto_bookmark.notes: Moves the editor viewport to a stored bookmark. This changes what a human is looking at, so it is not a neutral read — prefer editor_set_camera when you just need a viewpoint for a capture. NOT VERIFIED LIVE: described from the handler source.

params.name: path
params.description: Package FOLDER. Note this differs from blueprint_create / material_create / metasound_create, whose package_path is the full asset path with its last component discarded.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Full object path of the created ability blueprint — read it, given the path contracts differ between create commands

gas_create_ability.notes: Creates a UGameplayAbility blueprint. Lives in the optional HaybaMCPGAS satellite plugin, which auto-disables when the engine's GameplayAbilities plugin is off — so an Unknown command here means the satellite is not installed in this project, not that the command is missing. The ability is created empty; grant it to an actor with gas_grant_ability.

params.name: path
params.description: Package folder

params.name: duration_policy
params.description: Instant | HasDuration | Infinite

params.name: duration_seconds
params.description: Only meaningful with HasDuration

params.name: modifiers
params.description: Attribute modifiers: attribute, op, magnitude

gas_create_effect.notes: Creates a UGameplayEffect blueprint — the data asset that changes attributes, the unit GAS actually applies. duration_policy decides whether it fires once (Instant), ticks for a while (HasDuration) or persists until removed (Infinite). Part of the optional HaybaMCPGAS satellite.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Must own a UAbilitySystemComponent — a plain actor is refused by name

params.name: ability_path
params.description: Object path of a UGameplayAbility blueprint

fields.name: handle
fields.description: Granted-ability handle

gas_grant_ability.notes: Grants an ability to an actor's ability system component. It refuses an actor with no UAbilitySystemComponent rather than silently doing nothing, and refuses an uncompiled ability blueprint (no class default object) — both verified live. Grants made in the editor world are editor state, not gameplay state.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Must own a UAbilitySystemComponent

fields.name: active_handle
fields.description: Present for effects that persist; an Instant effect has none to return

gas_apply_effect.notes: Applies a gameplay effect to an actor's ability system component, for checking that an effect does what you think before wiring it into gameplay. Refuses an actor without an ability system component by name. An Instant effect changes attributes and leaves no active handle behind, so an empty handle is not a failure.

params.name: path_prefix
params.description: Filter by object-path prefix

fields.name: metasounds
fields.description: path, name, class

fields.name: capped
fields.description: True when the list was cut short — it says so rather than letting count disagree silently

metasound_list.notes: Enumerates MetaSound assets (sources and patches) from the asset registry. Part of the optional HaybaMCPMetaSound satellite; an Unknown command means the satellite is not installed.

params.name: package_path
params.description: Destination /Game folder, or the historic full intended asset path ending in name. Both spellings resolve to the same destination.

fields.name: path
fields.description: Where the asset ACTUALLY landed — check it against where you meant

fields.name: class
fields.description: MetaSoundSource

metasound_create.notes: Creates an empty MetaSoundSource asset. Author it with metasound_add_node/connect/set_input, inspect it, then use metasound_compile as the explicit validate/save boundary.

params.name: class_name
params.description: Registered MetaSound class name, for example Sine

params.name: namespace
params.description: Defaults to UE

metasound_add_node.notes: Adds a registered native MetaSound node and returns its stable node_id GUID. Mutates in memory; call metasound_compile to validate and save.

metasound_connect.notes: Connects two named pins using node GUIDs returned by add_node or inspect. Mutates in memory; call metasound_compile to validate and save.

params.name: type
params.description: float (default), int32, bool, or string

params.name: node_id
params.description: Omit to set a graph input default

metasound_set_input.notes: Sets a named node input default, or a graph input default when node_id is omitted. Mutates in memory; call metasound_compile to validate and save.

params.name: save
params.description: Defaults true

metasound_compile.notes: Conforms the asset to its document, initializes editor node locations, validates, and saves explicitly. Half-authored graphs are never implicitly saved by node edits.

metasound_inspect.notes: Read-only graph export with node GUIDs, named typed pins, edges, counts, and dirty state. Use before and after every mutation.

params.name: property_name
params.description: A UPROPERTY on the resolved actor, by reflection name

params.name: expected_value
params.description: Compared for equality. Numbers honour `tolerance`.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Editor label of the actor to inspect. Give this or actor_path.

params.name: actor_path
params.description: Full object path in the PIE world

params.name: tolerance
params.description: Float comparison slack — an exact match on a simulated float is rarely what you want

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Accepted for signature compatibility. It does NOT make the call wait — see the note.

fields.name: matched
fields.description: Whether the property equalled expected_value AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL

fields.name: observed_value
fields.description: Present on a match

fields.name: observed_value_last
fields.description: What was actually read, when it did not match — compare this against what you expected

fields.name: polling
fields.description: True when the answer is a single observation, i.e. a no-match. Poll again rather than treating it as final.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Why it did not match: a comparison miss, or pie_ended

editor_pie_assert.notes: Assert a UPROPERTY on a PIE actor holds a value. It is ONE OBSERVATION, not a wait: a command handler runs on the game thread, so it cannot advance the world, and a property it watches can never change while it blocks — an earlier version that pumped the ticker to fake waiting is what crashed the editor. So a false `matched` with `polling:true` means 'not yet', and the caller loops. Read observed_value_last before assuming the property is wrong; it is often the expectation that is.

params.name: actor_label
params.description: Give this or actor_path

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Accepted, but this call does not block — see the note

fields.name: polling
fields.description: True on a no-match: call again, the world will have advanced by then

editor_pie_wait_for.notes: The polling half of a PIE wait: one observation of a property, with `polling:true` when the condition is not met yet, so the caller can loop until it is or until it gives up. It does NOT block for you — the handler occupies the game thread it would need to advance, which is the reason the previous blocking version had to be removed. Same shape as editor_pie_assert; use this name when you intend to loop and that one when you intend a single check.
